comparable.client: AckProducer 4.3.2 (crash/client: kafka-clients from the pinned image, values padded to 1024 bytes), the same invocation against both systems; reads by kafka-console-consumer.sh

crash_modes.flakey-drop: SIGKILL of all three nodes at once, then every write the page cache had not flushed is dropped (dm-flakey drop_writes): power loss of the whole replica set

producer_props: every other producer setting at the client default

profiles.kafka-defaults: Kafka as shipped: no flush.messages, an acknowledgement is replication
profiles.kafka-fsync-parity: log.flush.interval.messages=1 on every broker and flush.messages=1 on the topic
profiles.vtop-group-commit-off: the shipped leader plus group_commit.enabled: false (each produce request has its own barrier)
profiles.vtop-group-commit-on: the shipped leader plus group_commit.enabled: true (concurrent produce requests share one fsync and one replication round)
profiles.vtop-shipped: node configuration as shipped (no group_commit section): acknowledged after a quorum (2 of 3) has fsynced; answers both Kafka profiles

comparable.simulation_limits: page-cache loss of one host for all three replicas at once; not a drive whose volatile cache lies about flushes, not a torn block, not independent crashes; the kernel can flush a little more between the kill and the drop (kill_to_drop_ms)

topology.kafka: 3 KRaft combined broker+controller nodes, RF=3, min.insync.replicas=2
topology.vtop: static range leader with the Kafka gateway plus two followers, quorum 2 of 3 (compose.vtop.yml); no metadata plane, so no election after the restart

configs.ack_producer_dockerfile:
# The crash benchmark's producer (#599): kafka-verifiable-producer's behaviour with a record size.
#
# The same KafkaProducer as the pinned apache/kafka image (its /opt/kafka/libs), compiled with the JDK that image
# lacks (it ships a JRE: no javac, no jshell), and copied onto that same image. The compiler stage is not in the
# result. Both bases are pinned by digest here; crash.py passes the same two values as build arguments, and a test
# keeps the three places equal.
ARG KAFKA_IMAGE=apache/kafka:4.3.2@sha256:852a0d49fc4e656b022e7f23785411802c9a088c78a7c5e39f33969de9c227a7
ARG JDK_IMAGE=eclipse-temurin:21.0.11_10-jdk@sha256:98155457fcdbeb0987472e8abf721657b698ede407aad52ac24ae42618c0931c

FROM ${KAFKA_IMAGE} AS kafka

FROM ${JDK_IMAGE} AS build
COPY --from=kafka /opt/kafka/libs /kafka-libs
COPY AckProducer.java /src/AckProducer.java
RUN mkdir /out && javac --release 21 -Xlint:all -Werror -cp "/kafka-libs/*" -d /out /src/AckProducer.java

FROM ${KAFKA_IMAGE}
COPY --from=build /out /opt/ackproducer
configs.kafka_compose:
# Apache Kafka for the head-to-head comparison (#595, #596): three brokers in
# KRaft mode, each a combined broker+controller, RF=3, min.insync.replicas=2.
#
# Fairness rule 1: every broker gets EXACTLY the limits each VTOP node gets in
# compose.vtop.yml (2 CPUs, 2 GiB, no swap, a named volume on the same Docker
# VM disk). Change one file, change the other; run.py records both in
# environment.json and refuses to start when they differ.
#
# Everything else is Kafka as shipped (profile `defaults`, #595 rule 4): no
# flush.messages, so a broker acknowledges on replication, not on fsync.
#
# The image is pinned by tag AND digest (rule 8); KAFKA_IMAGE overrides both.
name: kc-kafka

x-broker: &broker
  image: ${KAFKA_IMAGE:-apache/kafka:4.3.2@sha256:852a0d49fc4e656b022e7f23785411802c9a088c78a7c5e39f33969de9c227a7}
  cpus: 2
  mem_limit: 2g
  memswap_limit: 2g
  ulimits:
    nofile: { soft: 65536, hard: 65536 }
  # The same hardening as the VTOP nodes (fairness rule 1): no capabilities
  # (the broker listens above 1024 as appuser), no setuid gain. Not
  # read_only or pids_limit: the first would move the JVM's writable paths
  # to tmpfs, the second caps its threads; either could change what is
  # measured.
  cap_drop: [ALL]
  security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
  networks: [bench]
  healthcheck:
    test: ["CMD-SHELL", "/opt/kafka/bin/kafka-broker-api-versions.sh --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 > /dev/null 2>&1"]
    interval: 5s
    timeout: 20s
    retries: 30
    start_period: 10s

x-env: &env
  # One fixed id: KRaft formats every log dir with it on first start.
  CLUSTER_ID: "a2NvbXBhcmUtcGhhc2UtMQ"
  KAFKA_PROCESS_ROLES: "broker,controller"
  KAFKA_LISTENERS: "PLAINTEXT://:9092,CONTROLLER://:9093"
  KAFKA_CONTROLLER_LISTENER_NAMES: "CONTROLLER"
  KAFKA_INTER_BROKER_LISTENER_NAME: "PLAINTEXT"
  KAFKA_LISTENER_SECURITY_PROTOCOL_MAP: "CONTROLLER:PLAINTEXT,PLAINTEXT:PLAINTEXT"
  KAFKA_CONTROLLER_QUORUM_VOTERS: "1@kafka-1:9093,2@kafka-2:9093,3@kafka-3:9093"
  KAFKA_LOG_DIRS: "/var/lib/kafka/data"
  # The replication contract (#595 rule 3).
  KAFKA_DEFAULT_REPLICATION_FACTOR: "3"
  KAFKA_MIN_INSYNC_REPLICAS: "2"
  KAFKA_OFFSETS_TOPIC_REPLICATION_FACTOR: "3"
  KAFKA_TRANSACTION_STATE_LOG_REPLICATION_FACTOR: "3"
  KAFKA_TRANSACTION_STATE_LOG_MIN_ISR: "2"

  # a typo'd topic must not be auto-created with others.
  KAFKA_AUTO_CREATE_TOPICS_ENABLE: "false"

services:
  kafka-1:
    <<: *broker
    hostname: kafka-1

      <<: *env
      KAFKA_NODE_ID: "1"
      KAFKA_ADVERTISED_LISTENERS: "PLAINTEXT://kafka-1:9092"

  kafka-3:

    volumes: ["kafka-3-data:/var/lib/kafka/data"]

  kafka-2-data:
  kafka-3-data:

networks:

configs.kafka_crash_override:
# Kafka for the whole-replica-set crash benchmark (#599), layered on compose.kafka.yml.
#
# Only two things change, and neither touches what is measured:
#   - the three brokers' data directories are bind mounts under ${CRASH_DATA_ROOT} (one filesystem
#     for all three, so one crash is a simultaneous loss of all three replicas' page cache), as
#     named volumes whose driver options bind them there;
#   - the CPUs per broker come from ${CRASH_NODE_CPUS} (2, the base file's value, on the dedicated
#     host; the smoke run lowers it, for Kafka and VTOP alike).
# The bridge network gets its own name, so a crash run never collides with run.py or failover.py.

  kafka-1:
    cpus: ${CRASH_NODE_CPUS:-2}
  kafka-2:
    cpus: ${CRASH_NODE_CPUS:-2}
  kafka-3:
    cpus: ${CRASH_NODE_CPUS:-2}

    driver_opts: { type: none, o: bind, device: "${CRASH_DATA_ROOT:?set CRASH_DATA_ROOT}/kafka-1" }
  kafka-2-data:
    driver: local
    driver_opts: { type: none, o: bind, device: "${CRASH_DATA_ROOT:?set CRASH_DATA_ROOT}/kafka-2" }
  kafka-3-data:

networks:
  bench:
    name: kc-crash-kafka-bench
configs.kafka_fsync_parity_override:
# Kafka's `fsync-parity` profile (#595 rule 4): every broker flushes the log after every message, so
# an acknowledgement means "replicated AND on disk on the in-sync replicas". The topic gets
# flush.messages=1 as well, when crash.py creates it. Layered after compose.kafka.crash.yml.

  kafka-1:
    environment:
      KAFKA_LOG_FLUSH_INTERVAL_MESSAGES: "1"
  kafka-2:
    environment:
      KAFKA_LOG_FLUSH_INTERVAL_MESSAGES: "1"
  kafka-3:
    environment:
      KAFKA_LOG_FLUSH_INTERVAL_MESSAGES: "1"
configs.powercut:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# The host-level half of the whole-replica-set crash benchmark (#599): everything that needs root
# on the Docker host. crash.py runs it with `sudo -n` (or as root) and parses what it prints.
#
# WHAT THIS SIMULATES, precisely. The data directories of all three nodes of one system live on ONE
# ext4 filesystem on ONE device-mapper `flakey` device, which sits on a loop device over a sparse file.
# After the three processes have been SIGKILLed, `drop` reloads the flakey table with `drop_writes`
# WITHOUT freezing or syncing the filesystem (`--nolockfs`), so every write the page cache had not yet
# sent to the device is discarded, and `restore` unmounts, reloads a table that writes again, and
# mounts. What the filesystem holds afterwards is what had reached the device when the table was
# reloaded: data an fsync returned for, and whatever the kernel's own writeback had already flushed.
# That is the loss of the host's page cache for all three replicas at once (a kernel panic, or power
# loss with a disk that honours flushes).
#
# WHAT IT DOES NOT SIMULATE: a drive whose volatile write cache lies about flushes; a torn write
# inside one block; power loss of a host with a hardware write-back cache; independent crashes of the
# replicas (they share one failure domain on purpose); the instant between the kill and the drop (a few
# milliseconds, recorded as kill_to_drop_ms), in which the kernel may flush a little more, which can
# only make a system look better, never worse.
#
# Two canary files make every crash self-checking: one written with fsync completed (must be whole
# after the crash), one written with plain writes and no sync (must be absent or short when the cache
# is dropped).
#
# Usage: powercut.sh <command> <root> [args]     (root is the data root every node's directory is under)
#   setup <root> <size-mib>    create the image, the flakey device, an ext4 filesystem, mount it at <root>
#   teardown <root>            unmount and remove all of it
#   status <root>              print "flakey" if <root> is the mounted flakey device, "plain" otherwise
#   describe <root>            key=value lines for environment.json
#   sync <root>                flush that filesystem (before a crash, so only the load's data is at risk)
#   canary-synced <root>       write the canary that is fsynced
#   canary-unsynced <root>     write the canary that is not
#   canary-check <root>        print "synced=<bytes> unsynced=<bytes>"
#   drop <root>                drop every write from now on (after the SIGKILL)
#   restore <root>             unmount, write again, mount
set -euo pipefail

CANARY_BYTES=1048576

die() {
    echo "powercut: $*" >&2
    exit 1
}

command_name="${1:-}"
root="${2:-}"
[[ -n "$command_name" && -n "$root" ]] || die "usage: powercut.sh <command> <root> [args]"
root="${root%/}"
image="${root}.img"
state="${root}.flakey"
name="kc599-$(basename "$root")"
synced_file="${root}/.kc599-canary-synced"
unsynced_file="${root}/.kc599-canary-unsynced"

load_state() {
    [[ -f "$state" ]] || die "no flakey state at $state: run 'setup' first, or use a process-kill crash mode"
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    source "$state"
}

table_allow() { echo "0 ${sectors} flakey ${loopdev} 0 180 0"; }
table_drop() { echo "0 ${sectors} flakey ${loopdev} 0 0 180 1 drop_writes"; }

# Reload the flakey table without letting `dmsetup suspend` freeze and sync the filesystem: that sync
# would save exactly what a power loss loses.
reload_table() {
    local table="$1"
    dmsetup suspend --nolockfs --noflush "$name" 2>/dev/null || dmsetup suspend --nolockfs "$name"
    dmsetup load "$name" --table "$table"
    dmsetup resume "$name"
}

case "$command_name" in
setup)
    size_mib="${3:?setup needs a size in MiB}"
    [[ ! -e "$state" ]] || die "$state exists: a flakey device is already set up for $root"
    truncate -s "${size_mib}M" "$image"
    loopdev="$(losetup --find --show "$image")"
    sectors="$(blockdev --getsz "$loopdev")"
    dmsetup create "$name" --table "0 ${sectors} flakey ${loopdev} 0 180 0"
    mkfs.ext4 -q -F "/dev/mapper/${name}"
    mkdir -p "$root"
    mount "/dev/mapper/${name}" "$root"
    chmod 0777 "$root"
    printf 'loopdev=%q\nsectors=%q\n' "$loopdev" "$sectors" >"$state"
    echo "flakey device /dev/mapper/${name} on ${loopdev} (${sectors} sectors), ext4, mounted at ${root}"
    ;;
teardown)
    load_state
    umount "$root" 2>/dev/null || true
    dmsetup remove "$name" 2>/dev/null || true
    losetup -d "$loopdev" 2>/dev/null || true
    rm -f "$image" "$state"
    ;;
status)
    if [[ -f "$state" ]] && findmnt -n -o SOURCE "$root" 2>/dev/null | grep -q "/dev/mapper/${name}"; then
        echo flakey
    else
        echo plain
    fi
    ;;
describe)
    echo "kernel=$(uname -r)"
    echo "fs_type=$(findmnt -n -o FSTYPE --target "$root" 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
    echo "mount_options=$(findmnt -n -o OPTIONS --target "$root" 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
    echo "mount_source=$(findmnt -n -o SOURCE --target "$root" 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
    for key in dirty_expire_centisecs dirty_writeback_centisecs dirty_ratio dirty_background_ratio; do
        echo "vm.${key}=$(cat "/proc/sys/vm/${key}" 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)"
    done
    ;;
sync)
    sync -f "$root"
    ;;
canary-synced)
    dd if=/dev/zero of="$synced_file" bs="$CANARY_BYTES" count=1 conv=fsync status=none
    sync "$synced_file"
    sync "$root"
    ;;
canary-unsynced)
    dd if=/dev/zero of="$unsynced_file" bs="$CANARY_BYTES" count=1 status=none
    ;;
canary-check)
    synced=0
    unsynced=0
    [[ -f "$synced_file" ]] && synced="$(wc -c <"$synced_file" | tr -d ' ')"
    [[ -f "$unsynced_file" ]] && unsynced="$(wc -c <"$unsynced_file" | tr -d ' ')"
    echo "synced=${synced} unsynced=${unsynced}"
    rm -f "$synced_file" "$unsynced_file"
    ;;
drop)
    load_state
    reload_table "$(table_drop)"
    ;;
restore)
    load_state
    umount "$root" || die "cannot unmount $root: a process still holds it open; remove the containers first"
    reload_table "$(table_allow)"
    mount "/dev/mapper/${name}" "$root"
    ;;
*)
    die "unknown command ${command_name}"
    ;;
esac
configs.vtop_compose:
# VTOP for the head-to-head comparison (#595, #596): three data nodes from the
# image docker/Dockerfile builds, one range replicated to all three with a
# write quorum of 2 of 3, and the Kafka gateway on the range's leader.
#
# Fairness rule 1: EXACTLY the per-node limits compose.kafka.yml gives each
# Kafka broker (2 CPUs, 2 GiB, no swap, a named volume on the same Docker VM
# disk). run.py records both in environment.json and refuses to start when
# they differ.
#
# VTOP_IMAGE is set by run.py to the image it built from the commit under
# test (vtop-bench:<sha>), so the recorded commit is the one that ran.
name: kc-vtop

x-node: &node
  image: ${VTOP_IMAGE:?set VTOP_IMAGE to the vtop-bench image run.py built}
  entrypoint: ["vtop-node", "data", "--config", "/etc/vtop/node.yaml"]
  cpus: 2
  mem_limit: 2g
  memswap_limit: 2g
  ulimits:
    nofile: { soft: 65536, hard: 65536 }
  # The same hardening as compose.kafka.yml's brokers (fairness rule 1): no
  # capabilities (the node listens above 1024 as user vtop), no setuid gain.
  # Not read_only or pids_limit: the first would move writable paths to
  # tmpfs, the second caps threads; either could change what is measured.
  cap_drop: [ALL]
  security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
  networks: [bench]
  healthcheck:
    test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -sf http://127.0.0.1:9600/readyz > /dev/null"]
    interval: 2s
    timeout: 5s
    retries: 60
    start_period: 2s

services:
  # Followers first: the leader's quorum needs them listening.
  vtop-2:
    <<: *node
    hostname: vtop-2
    volumes:
      - "./vtop/follower-1.yaml:/etc/vtop/node.yaml:ro"
      # Mounted at the image's home (owned by the unprivileged `vtop` user), so
      # a fresh named volume inherits that ownership.
      - "vtop-2-data:/home/vtop"
  vtop-3:
    <<: *node
    hostname: vtop-3
    volumes:
      - "./vtop/follower-2.yaml:/etc/vtop/node.yaml:ro"
      - "vtop-3-data:/home/vtop"
  vtop-1:
    <<: *node
    hostname: vtop-1
    depends_on:
      vtop-2: { condition: service_healthy }
      vtop-3: { condition: service_healthy }
    volumes:
      # ${VTOP_LEADER_CONFIG} names another leader file: run.py's per-run group-commit config (#752) or crash.py's
      # group-commit configurations (#599); unset, it is the shipped one.
      - "${VTOP_LEADER_CONFIG:-./vtop/leader.yaml}:/etc/vtop/node.yaml:ro"
      - "vtop-1-data:/home/vtop"

volumes:
  vtop-1-data:
  vtop-2-data:
  vtop-3-data:

networks:
  bench:
    name: kc-vtop-bench
configs.vtop_crash_override:

# VTOP node 1: the range's static leader, with the Kafka gateway (#225).
#
# The shape scripts/live-chaos scenario 17 drives with a stock librdkafka
# client (a static leader at a fixed fencing epoch, two followers, quorum
# acknowledgement), moved into containers. Plaintext planes, as Kafka's
# PLAINTEXT listeners on the other side, so neither system pays for TLS; the
# `-on-any-interface` spelling is the node's own opt-in for leaving loopback.
#
# Every engine knob not written here is the binary's default (profile
# `defaults`, #595 rule 4): the gateway appends with Durability::Quorum, which
# acknowledges after a majority of the three replicas (leader included) has
# made the append locally durable (fsync) — 2 of 3, the write quorum the
# comparison asks for. Kafka under `defaults` acknowledges on replication
# without fsync; that difference is stated in the report, never hidden.
